tasks.title: Implement Netlify callback gateway and one-use Auth grants
tasks.body:
Goal:
- Provide the owner-selected Netlify Functions Free callback egress boundary without changing callback-secret custody or activating subscriptions.

Current behavior:
- Auth has no callback egress grant fence. The retained protocol prototype uses fake network adapters. The owner selected Netlify Functions Free; deployment and real callback execution require a concrete account and explicit scope.

Desired behavior:
- Supply a deployable dependency-free Node22 function and Auth/D1 one-use grant redemption. Auth authenticates exact dispatch bytes, destination, operation, audience, expiry and original request identity; the gateway verifies authority and atomically claims once before dispatch. Replay, lost claim acknowledgement and failed storage cannot cause another send.
- Resolve destinations immediately before a new TLS connection, reject private/special/mixed IPv4/IPv6 answers, pin one approved address, verify connected address and original hostname certificate, prohibit redirects and pooling, and bound time, headers, request and response bytes. Preserve exact signed webhook bytes.
- Keep callback URLs, bodies and signing headers transient; Auth stores only opaque grant identifiers, hashes and expiry. Workspace remains the later subscription/outbox/receipt owner. No callback signing key enters Netlify.

Touch:
- deploy/callback-egress Netlify function/configuration/tests, shared egress envelope, Auth narrow claim route/migration/default-off bindings and local security fixtures.

Discovery allowance:
- Verify current Netlify runtime/Free plan, Node TLS/DNS APIs and public-address registries. Existing repository pins remain unchanged.

Out of scope:
- Account provisioning, remote migrations, deployment, actual secrets or callbacks, subscription/vault lifecycle and application-event scheduling.

Implementation constraints:
- Use independent grant and claim authentication keys; no generic browser proxy. Fail closed for unsupported configuration. Public health reveals no secrets. Quota/unavailable responses preserve uncertainty and never select a paid/provider fallback.
- D1 supplies atomic single-use reservations across instances; no in-memory replay authority. Every network operation has an abort deadline and cleanup reserve. No production test CA or address-policy override.

Questions and required clarifications:
- [Resolved - owner selection] Netlify Functions Free; Auth-only callback signing/vault ownership. Local implementation is authorized by the resumed controller. Hosted activation remains a separate required task.

Validation:
- Production code tests cover IPv4/IPv6 special ranges, mixed/rebinding answers, actual controlled local TLS hostname/chain refusal, byte-for-byte signed payloads, redirects, deadlines/size limits, changed envelopes, concurrent replay, storage/acknowledgement loss, default-off configuration and secret-free results.
- Run affected Auth type/dry build before synthetic Miniflare/D1 checks. Prepare operator setup, bounded hosted profile and rollback. No actual endpoint security claim follows local tests.

Acceptance:
- The Netlify candidate and Auth single-use grant fence pass local destination, TLS, authentication, replay, uncertainty and size/deadline controls with exact signed bytes and no secret persistence or leakage.
- Deployable configuration and owner setup/rollback instructions preserve Free-plan limits, default-off operation and explicit hosted qualification requirements.

Documentation updates:
- Record candidate architecture, custody, retention, failure semantics, setup and local-versus-hosted evidence in technical/features/testing and a canonical callback egress contract.

Risks:
- Platform DNS/TLS behavior, cold starts, provider logging and quotas remain unqualified until the hosted task passes.

tasks.title: Qualify the selected Netlify callback gateway deployment
tasks.body:
Goal:
- Provide the owner-selected Netlify Functions Free callback egress boundary without changing callback-secret custody or activating subscriptions.

Current behavior:
- Auth has no callback egress grant fence. The retained protocol prototype uses fake network adapters. The owner selected Netlify Functions Free; deployment and real callback execution require a concrete account and explicit scope.

Desired behavior:
- Qualify the exact candidate on a selected owner Netlify Free account/site and matching Auth deployment using a bounded operator-approved profile. Record runtime, deployment/rollback identity, Free-plan hard limit, environment secret names, redacted provider logging configuration and permitted test destinations.
- Verify actual signed challenge bytes, public IPv4/IPv6 connection policy, controlled DNS changes, original-host TLS, redirect/private/mixed-address rejection, concurrency/replay, cold-start deadline and unavailable/quota behavior. Keep subscription activation unavailable until evidence passes.

Touch:
- Operator setup, selected Netlify/Auth deployment configuration and hosted evidence only; scoped repairs return to the existing implementation checkpoint.

Discovery allowance:
- Inspect connected provider access without exposing credentials. Obtain missing exact account/site, controlled fixture destinations and publication scope from the owner after the local candidate is reviewable.

Out of scope:
- Paid resources, automatic upgrades, provider fallback, real user callback enrollment, ChatGPT messages, subscriptions and gameplay.

Implementation constraints:
- Account creation, secret entry, remote migration and publication require explicit operator scope. No provider documentation or local TLS fixture substitutes for hosted acceptance. Do not probe unowned private services.

Questions and required clarifications:
- [Resolved - execution prerequisite] Netlify Functions Free is selected. The owner supplies the concrete account/site and hosted execution scope when the local implementation and profile are ready. No live access is inferred from the planning decision.

Validation:
- Execute the bounded hosted profile against owned fixtures after explicit scope; retain sanitized original receipts, negative controls, runtime/configuration and rollback evidence. Failed or unavailable controls leave the dependency incomplete.

Acceptance:
- The exact deployed gateway and Auth claim endpoint pass the approved hosted DNS/TLS, signed-byte, replay, deadline and unavailable/quota controls with sanitized evidence and a verified rollback path.

Documentation updates:
- Record actual hosted coverage and remaining host/device limitations; retain no real callback URL, signing material or account credentials.

Risks:
- Missing owner account, publication authority or controlled fixtures blocks execution. Free quota exhaustion must preserve undelivered state without paid fallback.
